title: SWF: custom ease curves (motionEaseCurve) not encoded in tween output
description: The Frame model in packages/core/src/model/types.ts has motionEaseCurve (line 178) and per-property ease curves (easeForPosition, easeForRotation, etc. lines 184-188). These are populated during FLA binary import. However, the SWF compiler (packages/swf/src/compile.ts) never references motionEaseCurve — it only uses the integer motionEase (-100..100) for classic easing. Flash 8 SWF encodes custom ease as multiple MotionTween action bytes or via the ScriptLimit tag approach. Actually, for Flash 8 SWF format, custom ease curves map to the Ease field in motion tween interpolation — but SWF tweening is implicit (the player interpolates between keyframes). The correct approach: when motionEaseCurve is present, sample it at N points to produce a lookup table and synthesize intermediate keyframes to approximate the custom ease, OR use Flash 8 per-property easing via DefineScalingGrid-adjacent approach. Research ruffle/swf/src to understand if SWF supports custom ease encoding; if not, sample the Bezier curve and insert synthetic keyframes in compile.ts. Priority: medium.
